items.title: Devils’ Anthony Mantha to ‘miss some time’ with throat injury
items.desc: The Devils went with 11 forwards and 7 defensemen for their game in Toronto on Sunday.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Devils forward Anthony Mantha will "miss some time" with a throat injury, and notes New Jersey dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen for its game in Toronto on Sunday.

The loss is real but not a crisis. Mantha has 10 points in 17 games so far this season, scoring five goals on 4.0 expected goals (the number of goals his chances should have produced), so he's running slightly hot. He plays 13.5 minutes a night, and the Devils have generated a bit less offense with him on the ice than without, by about 1.3 points of expected goal share. The team itself is strong: 12-5-0, with 59 percent of the expected goals. The weak spot is goaltending, where the group sits at minus 7.2 goals saved above expected so far this season.

Mantha has played every game so far, so we have no sample of the Devils without him. Going by how the coach has used his players, Connor Brown, at 14:26 a night, is next in line for his minutes. Mike Fink of The Hockey News posted that it will be interesting to see how Keefe handles the wing spot.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports two players went on waivers Saturday: Atro Leppanen and Rangers goalie James Reimer.

Reimer is the name most fans will know, and the move turned out to be a step toward the exit: The Hockey News later reported that the Rangers and Reimer had mutually agreed to terminate his contract. His only appearance this season came in relief, three goals on eight shots, and he finished last season 1.67 goals below expected over 14 games. At this stage of a long career, a waiver placement is rarely about another team claiming him and more often about clearing a path.

Leppanen hasn't played enough NHL hockey this season for our numbers to say anything useful about him.

items.title: Islanders’ Stanley fined for slashing Devils’ Hischier
items.desc: Logan Stanley delivered multiple whacks on Nico Hischier during New Jersey’s 5-4 OT win over New York on Saturday.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the NHL fined Islanders defenseman Logan Stanley for slashing Nico Hischier, after he delivered several whacks on the Devils center during New Jersey's 5-4 overtime win Saturday.

The two players involved tell you something about the night. Hischier is the engine of a 12-5-0 Devils team: New Jersey takes 62.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, about five points better than without him, and his 7 goals are right in line with his chances.

Stanley is in his first season on Long Island after playing for Winnipeg last year, averaging 21 minutes a night with 5 assists and no goals. The Islanders have been better with him on the ice, though they've also scored about 4.9 more goals than their chances deserve while he plays. Expect Hischier to see a lot more of him; these teams are in the same division.

items.title: Flames’ Kevin Bahl to miss rest of 2026-27 with ruptured Achilles tendon
items.desc: The Flames have placed Bahl on IR and recalled Brayden Pachal from the AHL’s Calgary Wranglers.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Flames defenseman Kevin Bahl will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with a ruptured Achilles tendon. Calgary put him on injured reserve and recalled Brayden Pachal from the AHL's Calgary Wranglers.

This hurts more than his two points in 16 games suggest. Bahl played almost 22 minutes a night, and the Flames' share of expected goals (the quality of chances) is about six points better with him on the ice than without. Calgary has controlled only 45% of the expected goals all season, and it just lost one of the reasons it wasn't worse.

Calgary is 7-9-1, and it can't afford to lose a regular. The minutes go to Zayne Parekh, who played a season-high 22:20 in the first game without Bahl and had two assists, and to Simon Nemec, who just signed a five-year extension. That's a younger, more offensive blue line. Whether it can defend without Bahl is the question now.

items.title: Report: Canadiens' Prospects Hage, Zharovsky 'Will Be Available' To The Team At The End Of The Season
items.desc: Montreal Canadiens star prospects Michael Hage and Alexander Zharovsky are expected to be available to join them at the end of the season, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reports.

stories.take:
The Hockey News, citing Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman, reports that Canadiens prospects Michael Hage and Alexander Zharovsky "will be available" to Montreal at the end of the season. In plain terms: when their current seasons finish, the Canadiens expect to be able to bring them in.

That's a good problem for an 11-3-3 team, but our numbers say the current group needs help more than the standings suggest. Montreal has 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) overall. The record leans on goaltending, which has saved 6.6 goals above expected. At five on five the share is a healthier 52%, so this isn't a mirage, but it's not a juggernaut either.

Prospects arriving in the spring rarely change a season. What it does is give Montreal options: in a playoff race, or a deep run, two skilled young forwards are a nice thing to have in reserve if the saves start to run out.

items.title: Leafs’ Morgan Rielly leaves game with lower-body injury
items.desc: Rielly left Saturday’s game against the Montreal Canadiens after just 5:45 of ice time.

stories.take:
Morgan Rielly left Saturday's loss to Montreal with a lower-body injury after only 5:45 of ice time, Daily Faceoff reports. There's no word yet on how long he'll be out.

The timing is rough for Toronto. The Leafs are 8-8-2, they've taken 47.19% of the expected goals this season (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and their 64 goals are 8.5 more than those chances usually produce. A team leaning on finishing can't afford to lose the players who tilt the ice, and Rielly does: Toronto's five-on-five expected-goals share is 2.23 points better with him on than off. His own line is quiet, 12 assists and no goals in 18 games, on 1.45 expected goals, so the goals should come if he's healthy. The Leafs play again tonight against a Devils team that has won four straight.

items.title: Oilers activate Zach Hyman, Devon Levi off IR
items.desc: Both Hyman and Levi have been out of the lineup for approximately two weeks due to various injuries.

stories.take:
Edmonton gets two pieces back at once: Daily Faceoff reports the Oilers have activated Zach Hyman and Devon Levi off injured reserve after about two weeks out.

Hyman matters most. He scored 31 goals in 58 games last season, much of it from the dirty areas beside Connor McDavid, and he has only one goal in seven games this year on 2.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances). That shortfall is small and should close. The Oilers haven't needed him much: they're 12-3-3 and have scored 19.39 more goals than their chances usually produce, which is the kind of finishing that tends to cool. Hyman's return is a hedge against that.

Levi, 7-1-0 with a .890 save rate and slightly below expected (-1.11), gives Edmonton its goaltending depth back. His high-danger save rate (.750 against a league .810) is the number we'd watch.

items.title: Rangers, James Reimer Contract Termination Echoes Historically Harsh Reality For Multiple Longtime NHL Goaltenders
items.desc: The New York Rangers have mutually agreed to terminate the contract of goalie James Reimer on Saturday. But while this is likely the end of Reimer's NHL career, his longevity is to be admired. Even the best goalies end their NHL careers in a non-ideal manner.

stories.take:
The Rangers and James Reimer have mutually agreed to terminate his contract, The Hockey News reports, and the outlet frames it as the likely end of his NHL career. It came a day after Daily Faceoff reported he had been placed on waivers.

The end was quiet on the ice too. Reimer appeared in one game this season, in relief, and allowed three goals on eight shots. Last season he played 14 games at 1.67 goals below expected. That is not how anyone in Toronto will remember him. A fourth-round pick of the Leafs in 2006, "Optimus Reim" became a cult favourite there before long stops across the league, and lasting as an NHL goalie for well over a decade is rare. As The Hockey News puts it, even the best goalies rarely get to leave on their own terms.

For New York, nothing changes in net. The Rangers' worry is finishing: 5.66 fewer goals than their chances usually produce.

items.title: Capitals’ Wilson ejected for boarding Panthers’ Vilmanis
items.desc: Wilson drilled the Florida defenseman from behind into the boards, resulting in a major penalty and a game misconduct.

stories.take:
Tom Wilson's afternoon ended early: Daily Faceoff reports he drove Sandis Vilmanis into the boards from behind and was given a major and a game misconduct. (Their report calls Vilmanis a defenseman; he plays forward for Florida.)

The question now is whether the league adds games. Wilson has been suspended before, more than once, and repeat offenders get longer bans. If he sits, Washington loses a 17-minute winger who hasn't been scoring (two goals on 4.97 expected) but is still a fixture on the top six, at 55.6% of the five-on-five expected goals. The Capitals showed Saturday they can survive a game without him, coming back from 2-1 down to win 4-3. A week or two without him is a different test.

items.title: Bruins place James Hagens on injured reserve
items.desc: The Bruins have called up Mike Eyssimont from their AHL affiliate, the Providence Bruins.

stories.take:
Boston has put James Hagens on injured reserve and called up Mike Eyssimont from Providence, Daily Faceoff reports. The reason hasn't been made public.

It's a loss the Bruins will feel. Hagens, the seventh overall pick in 2025, has 12 points (six goals) in 17 games while playing just 13:20 a night, a rate of 3.17 points per 60 that most veteran forwards would take. Our caution: his on-ice luck is running hot, with his teammates scoring well above their chances while he's out there, so some cooling was coming anyway. The bigger point is that Boston's 12-4-1 start rests on goaltending (12.6 goals saved beyond expected) more than on play, with the expected goals split close to even. Losing scoring depth makes that margin thinner.

items.title: Panthers’ Anton Lundell day-to-day with undisclosed injury
items.desc: Lundell has four goals and six points in 16 games with the Panthers in 2026-27.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports Anton Lundell is day-to-day with an undisclosed injury, and the outlet puts his line at four goals and six points through 16 games.

That line undersells him. At 5-on-5, Florida has taken 57.73% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Lundell on the ice, 5.19 points better than without him. The scoring hasn't followed because his linemates keep missing: his on-ice luck number sits at -5.17, meaning the goals while he plays trail the chances by about five. Last season he had 44 points in 64 games.

For a 9-5-2 Panthers team, a short absence costs them a center who drives play more than his points show. Day-to-day is the good version of this news.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Connor Hellebuyck, now with the Devils, addressed Jets fans for the first time since the trade, breaking his silence in an Instagram post about his decision to request a move out of Winnipeg.

The numbers say New Jersey is doing fine around him. The Devils are 10-5-0 and generate 58.6 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, with a strong 5-on-5 share of 58 percent. Hellebuyck's own start is the soft spot: three games, a .900 save percentage, and goals saved above expected of -0.54, meaning he has let in about half a goal more than an average goalie would have on the same shots. That is a tiny sample, and last season he was 3.43 goals better than expected over 57 games. Winnipeg, at 5-8-3, creates only 45.7 percent of the expected goals and has scored 9.6 fewer goals than its chances suggest. Its goaltending is roughly average (-0.1), so the Jets' problems sit mostly in play and finishing, not in net.

items.title: Dallas Stars GM Jim Nill Is Facing A Major Test With Jason Robertson's Next Contract
items.desc: Dallas Stars GM Jim Nill has managed his team's salary cap situation very well, but Jason Robertson's success could blow up their cap structure. How will the winger's next contract play out?

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Stars GM Jim Nill has handled Dallas's cap well, but that Jason Robertson's production could strain the structure when his next contract comes due. The same day, NHL.com's Tom Gulitti posted that Robertson scored the ninth-fastest hat trick to start a period in NHL history.

Our numbers say the production is real, if a touch hot. Robertson has 8 goals and 18 points in 15 games so far this season, and he's 2.31 goals above what his chances would predict. Expected goals measure the quality of chances, and his own sit at 5.7, so some of those 8 goals are finishing luck. The underlying play still holds up: DAL controls 56 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five when he's on the ice, and the team's share of the play is about 7 points better with him than without him. That's the kind of impact a team pays for, which is Nill's problem. Robertson went from 45 goals and 96 points last season, and he was drafted 39th overall in 2017, so the price has climbed steeply. DAL is 9-5-1, but its goals are 2.5 below expected and its goalies are 6.1 saved above expected, so the Stars need Robertson's driving to stay steady.
